videos.script: Every lesson in this course asks you to type a program and read what comes back. So this one starts by giving you somewhere to type. {{lab}} One Ubuntu machine, your own or a virtual one. A JDK from Ubuntu's archive, and two zip files: the Kotlin compiler and Gradle. Each one checked, each one asked what version it is. {{fails}} Then three ways that goes wrong, each made on purpose, each with a message that names its own cause. {{hello}} Then the first program. Three lines, a compiler that takes a few seconds, and a jar you can open to see what it made. {{val}} Then the first thing Kotlin does differently. Two words for a name: val, which never points anywhere else, and var, which can. The compiler holds you to the first. {{types}} And types. You will not write many, and every name still has one. You will see the compiler refuse to turn an Int into a Long without being asked. By the end you have a working machine, and a small program about one week of study.
